newsitem.title: LEBANON: France would veto non-francophone for U.N. - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France would veto non-francophone for U.N. - Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac acknowledged on Friday that U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali might not win re-election because of U.S. opposition and warned he would veto a non-French speaker.

Addressing students in Beirut, Chirac said he hoped the United States would not make good on its threat to veto Boutros-Ghali's candidacy when election procedures start next month ahead of the expiry of the 73-year-old Egyptian's first five-year term.

"I hope that will not be the case. It would be an additional element of crisis in the working of the United Nations, at a time when we need the U.N. to help solve the world's multiple problems and conflicts," he said.
"But if that were the case, then there will have to be a new candidate," the French leader said.
"France will not automatically veto any American candidate...but France would be prepared to veto any candidate who is not genuinely, normally francophone," he said.
Chirac noted that French was one of the official working languages of the United Nations and said he would insist that the secretary-general be a fluent French-speaker.
He paid tribute to Boutros-Ghali's "very remarkable work" in reforming the United Nations and said he was convinced a majority of U.N. member nations would vote to reappoint him.
But he said the five permanent members of the Security Council had the right to veto any candidate, which he was not calling into question.
The United States has insisted it is determined to block a second term for Boutros-Ghali, saying the United Nations needs new blood to drive a reform of its institutions more radically.
